title: Uncertainty ensemble
description: Parameter uncertainty, stored as a SAMPLE rather than a summary. A covariance matrix is a derived summary artifact, not the primary record: Gaussian summaries discard exactly the correlation structure that drives experimental design. Frequentist output declares itself as a sampling representation too -- a maximum-likelihood fit emits its point estimate plus a bootstrap or Laplace ensemble in this same shape -- so experiment design consumes ONE shape regardless of how the fit was done, and there is no need for two design pathways.

method.description: How the ensemble was produced. Required so that nobody mistakes an asymptotic approximation for a sampled posterior. Not a closed enum in 0.2.0 -- new methods are expected -- but must be one of the registered names or a documented extension.

method_family.description: The honest coarse label. laplace is asymptotic, bootstrap is resampled, hmc is sampled, a bare optimum is point. Downstream code that must not treat an asymptotic approximation as a posterior branches on this.

parameter_names.description: Column order of the sample array. Fixes the meaning of every column so a sample file is interpretable on its own.

parameter_units.description: Units per parameter, same order as parameter_names. Optional in 0.2.0 but strongly encouraged: a rate constant without a unit is not a rate constant.

parameter_transform.description: Whether the stored samples are in transformed space. Kinetic parameters are routinely fit in log space; leaving this implicit is a reliable way to be wrong by many orders of magnitude. 'mixed' means per-parameter -- read parameter_units; a thermodynamically-consistent fit carries log10 pre-exponentials beside linear enthalpies and entropies.

n_samples.description: Number of rows in the sample array. Declared here so a consumer can size a computation before fetching the bytes.

point_estimate.description: Same length and order as parameter_names. For a sampler, a chosen summary (posterior mean or MAP -- say which in notes). For a maximum-likelihood fit, the optimum.

samples.description: Pointer to the sample array, shape (n_samples, len(parameter_names)). Referenced indirectly like all bytes: an HMC run's samples can outgrow a repo.

log_density.description: Optional pointer to per-sample log posterior density or objective value.

summary_ref.description: Optional. The derived covariance or credible-interval summary computed FROM this ensemble. The direction of that arrow is deliberate.

identifiability.description: Optional. Which parameters are actually constrained by the data -- the M9 milestone is stated in terms of identifiable rate constants, so the field exists to be filled in rather than argued about later.

convergence.description: Optional, for sampled families: r_hat, ESS, divergences, seed.

conditioning.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch, for the September meeting. What this ensemble's spread conditions on. ABSENCE MEANS kind='conditional': the intervals are Type A evaluations (statistical, from the fitted observations alone, JCGM 100:2008) computed with every upstream quantity -- calibration chain, bed geometry, reconstructed inlet, transport correlations, feed -- held fixed at its point value, which is what every ensemble written before this field existed did silently. 'marginalized' means named nuisance quantities were integrated out against stated Type B inputs (calibration certificates, record-sourced priors), so the spread is a combined standard uncertainty in GUM's sense. 'profiled' means the named parameters were re-optimised at each evaluation point rather than integrated.

kind.description: conditional: everything not in parameter_names held fixed (Type A only). marginalized: the 'marginalized' list integrated out against Type B priors named in prior_source. profiled: the 'marginalized' list re-optimised per point.

held_fixed.description: Names of upstream quantities the intervals still condition on -- the honest remainder, whatever kind says. Naming them is the point: an unnamed conditioning is indistinguishable from none.

marginalized.description: Nuisance quantities integrated out (kind=marginalized) or profiled (kind=profiled), by name.

prior_source.description: Where the Type B inputs came from -- a calibration certificate, a record field (say which), or 'prior-free envelope' for the Lambda->0 bracket, which needs no prior at all and is the largest inflation any prior could produce.

parameter_roles.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. Role per parameter, same order as parameter_names. ABSENCE MEANS every parameter is 'interest', which is what every existing ensemble meant. Lets one artifact carry the joint (theta, phi) ensemble: 'interest' columns are the science, 'nuisance' columns are upstream quantities marginalized or profiled alongside them, 'derived' columns are functions of the others (a closure-computed reverse constant) whose spread is inherited rather than fitted.

parameter.description: The parameter of interest whose interval this row describes.

nuisance.description: The upstream quantity this row charges.

sensitivity.description: d(parameter)/d(nuisance) at the optimum -- the off-diagonal IFT block, in the parameter's stored transform per the nuisance's own units.

sigma_nuisance.description: The Type B standard uncertainty assigned to the nuisance, or null where none is stated in any record -- an honest null routes the row to the prior-free envelope instead of inventing a sigma.

contribution_decades.description: |sensitivity| * sigma_nuisance where sigma is stated: this nuisance's standalone contribution to the parameter's interval, in the stored transform's units. The column to sort by when deciding what to ask an experimentalist to measure.

source.description: Where sigma_nuisance came from (record field, certificate, assumption), or why it is null.

nuisance_budget.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. Ranked decomposition of interval width by upstream nuisance -- the costed ask list. Optional; meaningful alongside conditioning.kind='marginalized' or as a report on what a conditional interval IGNORES.

ensemble_id.description: The component ensemble this mixture resamples from.

weight.description: Mixture weight. Weights should sum to one across components.

weight_criterion.description: How the weight was computed (BIC, stacking, ...). Weights must come from refits, not from residuals at shared parameters -- divergence at fixed parameters did not survive refitting when that was measured here.

components.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. For a mixture over competing mechanisms or basins (method='posterior_mixture'): the component ensembles and their weights. The samples pointer then holds the weighted resample; this field is why it is reproducible.

approximation.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. The SHAPE assumption behind the spread, orthogonal to method_family: laplace and profile_likelihood are both 'asymptotic' there, but the first is quadratic around the optimum and the second follows the objective's actual shape -- erasing that distinction erases the reason to profile. ABSENCE asserts nothing, which is what every existing ensemble asserts.

notes.description: Which summary point_estimate holds (posterior mean, MAP, or optimum), and anything else a reader needs to interpret the ensemble correctly.

maturity.description: How much weight someone else may put on this record. Absent means `sandbox`, which is true of everything written before the field existed.
